# Requirement

* [NFR-001 Accessibility (M)](nfr-001.md) - NFR-001 requires WCAG 2.1 Level AA on the six listed screens, full keyboard operation and field errors associated with their fields; automated checks are recorded, the manual screen-reader and contrast pass is not.
* [NFR-002 Run locally](nfr-002.md) - The app runs on a developer machine with no cloud, hosted database or email service; the documented run steps and .env.example that the spec requires are deferred and absent at HEAD.
* [NFR-003 Responsiveness](nfr-003.md) - With up to 500 to-dos for one user, list, filter, search, page, create, edit, complete and delete results appear within 1 second in at least 95% of attempts.
* [NFR-004 Security baseline](nfr-004.md) - Passwords are hashed, input is validated on the server, no secrets are committed, and no response, error or log exposes stack traces, SQL, passwords or hashes.
* [NFR-005 Technology stack](nfr-005.md) - The UI is React with TypeScript, the API is Java with Spring Boot, the browser talks to the API over HTTP, and storage is SQLite.
* [NFR-006 User-friendly error messages](nfr-006.md) - Every failure the web app shows is a plain-language message with a next step and no technical internals, and an unexpected error in the app shows a recoverable page.
* [NFR-007 Modular API](nfr-007.md) - The API is one Spring Boot application and one SQLite pool, split into an identity module and a to-dos module whose boundaries, cycles and endpoint ownership are checked by tests.
* [REQ-ACC-001 Overall success scenario](req-acc-001.md) - The end-to-end scenario covers add, see, search, filter, edit, complete and delete for one user, isolation from a second user, and persistence across an API restart.
* [REQ-AUTH-001 Self sign-up](req-auth-001.md) - A new person creates an account with one identifier, an email address or a username, and a password, with no email verification step.
* [REQ-AUTH-002 Login](req-auth-002.md) - A registered user logs in with identifier and password, gets an 8-hour session that survives a reload, and sees the same generic refusal for a wrong password and an unknown identifier.
* [REQ-AUTH-003 Password storage](req-auth-003.md) - Passwords are stored only as salted one-way hashes from a strong algorithm, and no password or hash appears in any response or log line.
* [REQ-AUTH-004 Unauthenticated access and logout](req-auth-004.md) - Every to-do operation is refused without a valid session, logout ends the session, and an ended session sends the user to log in with a session-ended message.
* [REQ-AUTH-005 No admin role](req-auth-005.md) - The system has one role with identical permissions for every account, and no operation lists users or reads another user's to-dos.
* [REQ-DATA-001 Persistence](req-data-001.md) - All accounts and to-dos, with their status, due date, priority and timestamps, survive an application restart in a SQLite file that is created on first start.
* [REQ-DATA-002 Concurrent edits, last write wins](req-data-002.md) - Two edits to the same to-do are both accepted with the later write stored and no conflict error, and edits to different to-dos are stored independently.
* [REQ-ISO-001 Per-user isolation](req-iso-001.md) - A user sees, searches, changes and deletes only their own to-dos, and another user's identifier gets the same not-found as a missing one.
* [REQ-LIST-001 Filter by status](req-list-001.md) - The list filters to All, Active or Completed to-dos, defaults to All, and shows a no-matches state when the chosen filter matches nothing.
* [REQ-LIST-002 Search](req-list-002.md) - Search matches the text of titles and descriptions case-insensitively as a literal substring, combines with the filter, treats whitespace-only text as no search, and never errors on special characters.
* [REQ-LIST-003 Pagination](req-list-003.md) - The list shows 20 to-dos per page in a stable newest-first order, with Previous and Next controls, a page past the last clamped to the last valid page, and a 400 for zero, negative or non-numeric pages.
* [REQ-NAV-001 Home route and not-found page](req-nav-001.md) - The root address goes to the to-do list, an undefined address shows a signed-in user an accessible not-found page with a link home, and signed-out visitors are sent to log in.
* [REQ-TODO-001 Create a to-do](req-todo-001.md) - A signed-in user creates a not-done to-do with a title, a due date, an optional priority (default Medium) and an optional description, which appears first in their list.
* [REQ-TODO-002 To-do field rules and validation](req-todo-002.md) - Titles are trimmed to 1 to 200 characters, descriptions are at most 2000, the due date is a required real calendar date, and priority is Low, Medium or High, with the server refusing anything else.
* [REQ-TODO-003 View and order the list](req-todo-003.md) - The list shows each user's to-dos newest first with title, done status, due date and priority, a first-use empty state, and each to-do's detail with description and timestamps.
* [REQ-TODO-004 Edit a to-do](req-todo-004.md) - A user edits title, description, due date and priority of their own to-do; valid saves persist and advance the updated time, invalid saves change nothing, and a missing to-do gives not-found.
* [REQ-TODO-005 Mark done and not done](req-todo-005.md) - A user toggles a to-do between Active and Completed, the change persists with an advanced updated time, and the Active view drops a newly completed to-do without a page reload.
* [REQ-TODO-006 Delete a to-do](req-todo-006.md) - Deleting asks for confirmation, removes the to-do permanently, returns not-found for it afterwards, and falls back to the last valid page when the last to-do on a page is deleted.
* [REQ-TODO-007 Clear all completed](req-todo-007.md) - A user deletes all of their Completed to-dos, across pages and filters, after a confirmation that states the count, with the control disabled when there are none.
